analysis.investment_thesis: CEAT passes the ROIC screen (~22% on invested capital) but fails the earnings yield screen at only 8.6% (EBIT ₹1,475 Cr / EV ₹17,079 Cr), making it half a Magic Formula stock at best. It is a capital-intensive commodity business in a competitive industry — exactly the kind that rarely shows up in my top rankings.
key_strengths: ROIC of ~22% (EBIT ₹1,475 Cr / invested capital ₹6,660 Cr) clears the 20% threshold; ROCE of 15.4% confirms disciplined capital use
Revenue growing at 10.3% 9-year CAGR with EBITDA expanding from ₹756 Cr (2022) to ₹1,513 Cr (2025), showing recovery from a cyclical trough
OCF positive all 5 of 5 years with operating CF ₹1,092 Cr in 2025; D/E of 0.68 is manageable
key_risks: Earnings yield of only 8.6% means you're paying full price for a cyclical business — far below my 12% minimum threshold for attractiveness
Capex of ₹943 Cr in 2025 devoured nearly 86% of OCF; FCF was a thin ₹149 Cr on ₹13,218 Cr revenue — this is not a capital-light compounder
Finance costs growing at 11.9% CAGR (₹278 Cr in 2025), outpacing EBIT growth and eroding equity returns
red_flags: Borrowings surged from ₹1,792 Cr (2024) to ₹3,114 Cr (2025) — a 74% jump in one year with no clear explanation in the data
Net profit CAGR of only 0.9% over 9 years despite 10.3% revenue growth — the operating leverage is not flowing to shareholders
Operating margin of 9% is thin for the risk; peer-to-peer competition in tyres prevents meaningful pricing power
analysis.detailed_analysis: Applying the Magic Formula: EV = ₹14,991 Cr market cap + ₹2,136 Cr net debt − ₹48 Cr cash = ~₹17,079 Cr. EBIT (operating income) of ₹1,475 Cr gives an earnings yield of 8.6% — disappointing, well below the 12% I need to get excited. ROIC of ~22% is decent and passes the quality screen, but you need both legs to work for a strong ranking. CEAT is a subsidiary of RPG Enterprises selling tyres in a commodity market where rubber prices drive margins more than management skill.
